coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks
record.distance_note: Piers 68 & 70's dry-dock and ship-repair facility sits immediately north of Brookfield's tracked 28-acre Pier 70 redevelopment parcel and Crane Cove Park, outside both -- Port materials describe it as a separate 13-acre facility, closed in 2017, at the complex's northeast corner.

how_to_comment.channel: Clerk of the Board of Supervisors

record.summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is stabilizing both structures and plans to demolish and dispose of them, at a total estimated cost of $61.2M, of which about $20.0M was secured as of February 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- two hand-traced hull outlines from satellite imagery, accurate to a few metres at best, not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is inferred from their measured lengths against the 900 ft the Port memo gives for Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka lengths Mission Local (528 ft) and Potrero View (570 ft) give, which disagree; no source read places them. The outlines cover the two floating hulls only, not the 13-acre shipyard: the Pier 68 wharf arms, the quay, the cranes, the sheds and four unidentified floating tank sections west of the Eureka are left out. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: Assessor lot: both hulls lie inside lot 9900068 (98% of the outline). DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset (acdm-wktn), queried by lot number on 2026-10-10 and read again on 2026-10-11, lists Assessor lot 9900068 in block 9900 (lot 068), marked active, with a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02. The dataset's own description of its recorded-drop-date column reads 'This is the date that the documents related the to dropping/retiring of the parcel was recorded, as tracked by Public Works.' The same row has no map-drop date, is flagged active, and is on the Assessor's secured roll in the copy dated 2026-10-01. The dataset does not say why a recorded drop date and an active flag appear together, so this record states only what the row shows. The lot is the whole shipyard lot, not an outline of the two hulls: the traced hulls cover 18% of it. Port structures carry no street name in that dataset, so a search for PIER-numbered street names finds nothing. Outline: two hand-traced hull outlines -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29). The earlier placeholder box lay in open water north of the shipyard. Hulls were told apart by length. The Port Commission memo (Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09, PDF p. 3) says: 'DD2 is a 900-foot single-section steel floating dry dock constructed by the Bethlehem Steel Corporation in 1970.' Mission Local (2026-02-23) says: 'Dry Dock No. 2, which was built in 1970, ...' and 'The adjacent dry dock, Eureka, which was built in 1945, is 528 feet long'. Potrero View (2026-07-15) gives the Eureka as longer: 'Eureka Drydock is 570 feet.' The sources disagree on the Eureka's length (528 ft is 161 m; 570 ft is 174 m) and agree on its 1945 build. The large eastern hull measures about 283 m (Dry Dock No. 2: 900 ft is 274 m) and the central hull about 169 m including wing walls, so the central hull is the shorter dock whichever Eureka length is right. No source read says which hull sits where, so this match is Pier & Point's own inference. Still no Port GIS layer or site-plan figure to trace from.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Both hulls lie inside Assessor lot 9900068, the whole shipyard lot (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, checked 2026-10-10 and again 2026-10-11), which this record does not use as an outline because the hulls cover only 18% of it. That row carries a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02 yet reads active; see 'Traced from' above.
notes.regulatory_context: Dry Dock No. 2 (a 900-foot floating dry dock built in 1970) developed excessive listing after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding in November 2025; the Port Commission President and Executive Director declared an emergency on 2025-12-08 (Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09). Port staff anticipate advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026 for Dry Dock No. 2 and the neighboring Eureka Dry Dock (a second floating dry dock at Piers 68/70, formerly USS Steadfast/AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP). Total estimated cost of stabilization and disposal is $61.2M (Capital Planning Committee memo, 2026-02-09); see the record file for the funding breakdown and what remains unfunded.

facts.value: Two floating dry docks: Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (the latter formerly USS Steadfast, AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka preserved at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP)

Built in 1945. Its length is reported as 528 feet by Mission Local and 570 feet by Potrero View; the Port memo gives no length (see open questions)

costs.what: Cap on emergency stabilization work (continuous pumping, reinforcing steel, stabilizing deck cranes) authorized under the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration

Total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (Phase 1A stabilization $8.6M + Dry Dock No. 2 disposal $27.4M + Eureka disposal $15.7M + $9.5M contingency, per the Capital Planning Committee's Feb 2026 cost table); about $20.0M was secured as of Feb 2026, with roughly $41.2M pending FY2026-27 budget approval

milestones.text: Potrero View reports the Port has directed an outside engineering firm to prepare preliminary engineering plans for demolition of both dry docks and help secure permits; a Port spokesperson is quoted saying the package will be used "to advertise for a future design-build contract". Separately, in its own words rather than as a quotation, Potrero View says the Port expects initial plans to be completed by March 2027 and a demolition contract tendered in the second half of 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View). This is later than the summer 2026 advertising the January 2026 Port memo anticipated.

open_questions: The Eureka Dry Dock's length is given as 528 feet by Mission Local (2026-02-23) and as 570 feet by Potrero View (2026-07-15); the Port's January 2026 memo gives no length for it, so neither figure is shown as settled here. Both sources give 1945 as its build year and 900 feet and 1970 for Dry Dock No. 2.

Whether the $18.5M Port Commission Resolution 24-51 authorization (Oct 2024) is a subset of, or additional to, the $61.2M total cost figure presented in the Feb 2026 Capital Planning Committee memo is not established by the sources reviewed here.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.

Has the Port advertised or awarded a demolition contract for the dry docks? As of 2026-10-10 no Port Commission item or Port contract notice was found reporting an advertisement or award; the July 2026 Potrero View report describes the design-build contract as still to come.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.
